summary: Skoda's compact electric SUV undercuts every other European EV on price in Australia and reviewers consistently rate its efficiency, DC charging speed and conventional, button-rich cabin as class-leading. The split verdict is on ride and range: Australian testers find the fixed-rate suspension too firm for patchy suburban tarmac, and the entry 60 Select's sub-400km WLTP claim asks buyers to pay $7,000 more for the 85 Select to get genuine touring range. Cheap prepaid servicing and a seven-year warranty offset an equipment list that still omits surround-view cameras, sat-nav and a connected app.
pros: 60 Select lists at $48,990 before on-roads, making it the cheapest European-built EV on sale in Australia and priced against Chinese rivals like the BYD Atto 3 and Geely EX5
Genuinely efficient: CarsGuide's long-term 60 Select averaged 15.9kWh/100km, exactly matching the WLTP claim, and CarExpert saw 12.8kWh/100km in the 85
Fast DC charging for the money - the 60 Select peaks at 165kW for 10-80 per cent in about 24 minutes, the 85 at 175kW in about 28 minutes
Prepaid servicing works out to roughly $195 a year over 10 years, with a 7-year/unlimited-km warranty
Rear-drive chassis, 9.3m turning circle and retained physical climate controls; 470L boot expanding to 1580L with Skoda's usual clever storage
cons: Suspension is tuned too firmly for Australian roads - reviewers report a busy, thumping ride over road joins, and no adaptive dampers are offered on Select grades
60 Select's 395km WLTP range is sub-400km; a real-world long-term test returned only 371km, so the 85 Select's 529km costs an extra $7,000
No ANCAP rating as at July 2026 - it relies on a 2025 five-star Euro NCAP result, which can be a blocker for fleet and novated-lease policies
Select grades go without surround-view camera, satellite navigation, vehicle-to-load and a spare tyre, and lack the connected app, remote climate and over-the-air updates rivals include
Lane-keeping assistance is over-sensitive and needs resetting each drive, a common complaint across Australian first drives
